newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania lists 128 state firms for privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania lists 128 state firms for privatisation.

text.p: Tanzania has earmarked 128 state-owned firms for privatisation by the end of next year as part of Western-backed economic reforms in the formerly socialist country, a senior official said on Monday.
The official at the Parastatal Sector Reform Commission (PSRC) told Reuters 31 of the firms would be sold by the end of this month, with the total rising to 78 by the end of the year.
"We're working on a two-year rolling plan," said the official who declined to be named.
He said a detailed list and timetable for the privatisation exercise would be made public within a fortnight.
Tanzania is scheduled to open a stock exchange later this month. The Capital Markets and Securities Authority last week invited private companies to prepare prospectuses in readiness for the opening.
Tanzania Breweries, owned jointly by a South African firm and the Tanzanian government, is among firms slated for listing.

The official said other candidates include National Steel Corporation, the National Bicycle Company, Motor Mart, National Engineering Company, Tanzania Cables Limited, Southern Paper Mills, Ubungo Farm Implements and Machine Tools Limited.

Tanzania first embarked on privatisation of some 400 cash-strapped state firms in 1993 as part of western-backed economic reforms but critics including key donors say the programme has been too slow and is fraught with corruption.
Western donors underwrite annual aid of over $800 million to this impoverished east African nation and normally tie fund disbursement to continuation of reforms.
